en: to be absent from work; to call in sick

examples.ko: 연락 없이 결근한 탓에 팀장님께 꾸중을 들었어요.
examples.en: I got scolded by my team leader because I was absent without notice.

examples.ko: 감기가 심해서 오늘은 결근을 해야 할 것 같아요.
examples.en: My cold is bad, so I think I have to take today off work.
Why were you absent from work yesterday?

examples.ko: 이번 달에 한 번도 결근하지 않았어요.
examples.en: I haven't missed a single day of work this month.
If you miss work because you're sick, you need to call ahead.
That employee is often absent, so I'm worried.

explain: 회사에 와야 하는데 오지 않는 것에 써요. 학교에 안 가는 것은 '결석하다'라고 해요. 허락받고 쉬는 것은 보통 '휴가를 내다', '연차를 쓰다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I was absent from work yesterday because I was sick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 일어난 일을 말하는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense for something that already happened.

phrases.en: You must not be absent from work without notice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙이나 충고를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for rules or advice.

phrases.en: I called my team leader in the morning to say I'd be absent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에 못 간다고 미리 알리는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means telling your workplace you can't come in.

explain_en: It is used when you are supposed to be at work but do not show up. Missing school is '결석하다'. Taking approved time off is usually '휴가를 내다' or '연차를 쓰다'.

examples.en: I grilled and ate saury for dinner tonight.
I made tasty kimchi stew with canned saury.
I heard autumn saury tastes the best.

examples.ko: 꽁치는 뼈가 많아서 조심해서 먹어야 해요.
examples.en: Saury has many bones, so you have to eat it carefully.
I bought three saury at the market.
I served the grilled saury with grated radish.

explain: 몸이 길고 가늘어서 고등어와 모양이 달라요. 생선구이로도 먹지만 '꽁치 통조림'으로 찌개를 끓여 먹는 일도 많아요. 생선은 '한 마리, 두 마리'로 세요.

phrases.en: Grilled saury with rice is really delicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생선을 구워 먹는 가장 흔한 방법을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names the most common way of grilling and eating the fish.

phrases.en: Today I made saury stew.
phrases.nuance_ko: 통조림 꽁치로 많이 끓이는 집밥 메뉴예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A home-cooked dish often made with canned saury.

phrases.en: I bought two saury at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생선을 세는 단위 '마리'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the counter '마리' for fish.

explain_en: It has a long, slim body, so it looks different from mackerel. It is eaten grilled, but many people also make stew with canned saury ('꽁치 통조림'). Fish are counted as '한 마리, 두 마리'.

examples.en: It takes about an hour to get to the destination.
Enter the destination in the taxi app first.
The destination is Seoul Station and the departure point is Busan Station.
Contact me when you get off at your destination.
We had lunch somewhere near the destination.
If we're going to the same place, let's take a taxi together.

explain: 교통, 택배, 길 안내에서 많이 써요. 반대말은 '출발지'예요. 비슷한 '목적지'는 가려는 곳이라는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: Please write both the departure point and the destination.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말과 함께 짝으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as a pair with its opposite.

phrases.en: Please check the delivery destination address.
phrases.nuance_ko: 택배나 배달에서 받을 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the receiving address in deliveries.

phrases.en: I go to my destination by bus.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도착지'보다 가려는 마음이 담긴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Carries more of a sense of the place you intend to go.

explain_en: It is common in transport, deliveries and navigation. The opposite is '출발지'. The similar '목적지' leans more toward the place you intend to go.

examples.en: I switch my phone to airplane mode.

examples.ko: 무음 모드라서 전화 소리가 안 났어요.
examples.en: The phone didn't ring because it was on silent mode.
If you change the screen mode, it is easier on the eyes.

examples.ko: 공부 모드에 들어가면 휴대폰을 안 봐요.
examples.en: When I go into study mode, I don't look at my phone.
This game has two modes.
Dark mode is good to use at night.

explain: 영어 mode에서 온 말이에요. 휴대폰이나 게임에서 '비행기 모드', '무음 모드'처럼 설정 상태를 말해요. '공부 모드'처럼 사람의 상태를 가볍게 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The battery was low, so I switched to power saving mode.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰이나 컴퓨터 설정 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the settings of a phone or computer.

phrases.en: It's exam season, so I'm in study mode these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 상태를 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used casually to describe a person's state.

phrases.en: Let's try changing the game mode.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설정을 다른 것으로 바꿀 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for switching to a different setting.

explain_en: It comes from English 'mode'. On phones and games it names a setting, as in '비행기 모드' or '무음 모드'. People also say '공부 모드' lightly for their own state.

examples.en: A driver's license must be renewed within the deadline.

examples.ko: 렌터카를 빌릴 때는 여권과 면허증을 같이 보여 줘야 해요.
examples.en: When renting a car, you have to show your passport and license together.
I lost my wallet and had my license reissued.

examples.ko: 면허증 사진이 십 년 전 거라서 지금 얼굴과 너무 달라요.
examples.en: My license photo is from ten years ago, so it looks very different from my face now.

examples.ko: 직원이 면허증으로 본인 확인을 한 뒤에 차 열쇠를 줬어요.
examples.en: The staff member verified my identity with my license and then gave me the car key.

explain: '-증(證)'은 신분이나 자격을 증명하는 카드예요: 학생증, 신분증, 면허증. 운전면허는 '따다'라고 해서 '면허를 따다'라고 하고, 카드 자체는 '면허증'이라고 해요.

dict_examples.ko: 교통 신호를 위반한 운전자에게 경찰은 면허증을 제시하라고 하였다.
dict_examples.en: The police told the driver who had violated the traffic signal to show his license.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: -증 (證) marks a card that proves identity or qualification: 학생증 (student ID), 신분증 (ID), 면허증 (license). You 'get' a license with 따다 (면허를 따다), and the card itself is the 면허증.

examples.en: Korea exports cars to many countries.
This company exported fruit last year.
It's a product exported overseas, so the packaging is sturdy.
They are exporting seaweed to many countries.
You need a lot of documents to export goods.

examples.ko: 작년에 수출한 양이 두 배가 됐어요.
examples.en: The amount exported last year doubled.

explain: 짝말은 '수입하다'예요. 나라 밖으로 내보내면 '수출', 안으로 들여오면 '수입'이라서 소리가 비슷해 헷갈려요. '출'은 나가는 것, '입'은 들어오는 것으로 기억하세요.

phrases.en: Our company exported clothes last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 이미 나라 밖으로 내보낸 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used for something already sent out of the country.

phrases.en: Car exports increased this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수출이 많아졌다고 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for saying exports have grown.

phrases.example: 이 회사는 외국에 물건을 수출하지 않아요.
phrases.en: This company does not export goods abroad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 수출하지 않는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say a company does not export.

explain_en: Its counterpart is '수입하다'. Sending goods out of the country is '수출' and bringing them in is '수입', and the similar sounds are easy to mix up. Remember '출' as going out and '입' as coming in.

examples.en: I stayed overnight at a friend's house last night.
My parents do not like me staying out overnight.
If you want to stay out overnight, tell your mom first.
Soldiers can stay out overnight on weekends.
My son stayed out overnight without a word, so I was worried.
Is it okay if I stay out overnight tomorrow?

explain: 여행 가서 자는 것은 보통 '외박'이라고 하지 않고 '숙박'이나 '묵다'를 써요. 외박은 집에 들어가지 않고 다른 곳에서 밤을 보낸다는 느낌이 강해서 부모님, 기숙사, 군대 이야기에 써요.

phrases.en: I stayed out overnight at a friend's house yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '외박하다'를 둘로 나눈 말로, 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: This splits 외박하다 in two; the meaning is the same.

phrases.en: Please don't stay out overnight from the dormitory.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙이나 부탁을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for rules or requests.

phrases.example: 엄마, 오늘 친구 집에서 외박해도 돼요?
phrases.en: Mom, can I stay out overnight at a friend's house today?
phrases.nuance_ko: 허락을 구할 때 '-아/어도 돼요?'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-아/어도 돼요?' to ask for permission.

explain_en: Sleeping somewhere on a trip is not usually called '외박'; people say '숙박' or '묵다'. '외박' feels like not coming home and spending the night elsewhere, so it fits talk about parents, dormitories and the military.

examples.ko: 인스턴트식품을 너무 자주 먹으면 건강에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Eating instant food too often is bad for your health.
Instant food is convenient, but a lot of it is salty.
When I'm busy, I get by on instant food.

examples.ko: 인스턴트식품 대신 직접 요리해 먹기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to cook for myself instead of eating instant food.
The fridge is full of instant food.
What kinds of things count as instant food?

explain: 라면, 즉석밥, 냉동식품처럼 간단히 조리해서 먹는 음식을 말해요. '즉석식품'이라는 말도 비슷하게 써요. 건강 이야기에서는 조금 부정적인 느낌으로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: When I'm busy, I eat instant food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation.

phrases.en: I'm cutting down on instant food for my health.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건강 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in health talk.

phrases.en: Ready-made food only needs to be heated.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word used in a similar way.

explain_en: It covers food that is simple to prepare, like ramen, instant rice and frozen food. '즉석식품' is a similar term. In talk about health it often carries a slightly negative feel.

examples.ko: 엄마가 아이를 새 어린이집에 천천히 적응시켜요.
examples.en: The mother helps her child adjust slowly to the new daycare.

examples.ko: 새 직원을 빨리 업무에 적응시키려고 해요.
examples.en: We're trying to get the new employee used to the work quickly.

examples.ko: 강아지를 새 집에 적응시키는 데 일주일 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a week to get the puppy used to the new home.

examples.ko: 식물을 추운 날씨에 적응시키면 더 튼튼해져요.
examples.en: If you acclimate plants to cold weather, they get sturdier.

examples.ko: 선수들을 새 환경에 적응시킨 뒤 경기를 시작했어요.
examples.en: They started the game after getting the players used to the new environment.

examples.ko: 몸을 더위에 적응시켜서 운동 시간을 늘려요.
examples.en: I get my body used to the heat and then increase my exercise time.

explain: '적응하다'는 내가 맞추는 것이고, '적응시키다'는 다른 사람이나 동물, 식물이 맞추게 도와주는 것이에요. '-을/를 -에 적응시키다'로 써요.

phrases.example: 선생님이 아이들을 새 교실에 적응하게 해요.
phrases.en: The teacher helps the children adapt to the new classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: '적응시키다'와 같은 뜻을 풀어서 말하는 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way of spelling out the same meaning as 적응시키다.

phrases.example: 강아지를 새 집에 익숙해지게 해 주세요.
phrases.en: Please help the puppy get used to its new home.
phrases.nuance_ko: '익숙하다'를 써서 더 쉽게 말하는 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler way to say it using 익숙하다.

phrases.en: A senior colleague helps the new employee adjust.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도와주는 일에 초점을 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses on the act of helping someone adjust.

explain_en: '적응하다' is you adjusting yourself, whereas '적응시키다' is helping another person, animal, or plant adjust. The pattern is '-을/를 -에 적응시키다'.

p.n: 적응하다 cannot take 아이를 here; the subject and object would have to change.

examples.en: The place I live in now is a jeonse home.
I went to a real estate office to find a good jeonse home.
My jeonse contract ends next month.
We began our married life in a small jeonse home.

examples.ko: 전셋집은 마음대로 벽에 못을 박기 어려워요.
examples.en: In a jeonse home it's hard to hammer nails into the wall as you like.
I heard a jeonse home became available near the office.

explain: '월세방'처럼 매달 월세를 내는 집과 구분할 때, 또 '내 집'과 구분할 때 써요. 전세는 한국에서 쓰는 독특한 집 계약 방식이라서 번역보다 그대로 '전세'로 기억하는 게 좋아요.

phrases.en: My current home is a jeonse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집 계약 방식 자체를 말하는 말이고, '전셋집'은 그 집을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: It names the contract type itself, while '전셋집' means the home.

phrases.en: I'm looking for a new jeonse home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이사할 집을 찾을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you are looking for a place to move into.

phrases.en: The newlywed couple lives in a jeonse home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 집이 아니라 전세로 사는 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes living on a jeonse lease rather than in a home you own.
phrases.en_equiv: to live in a jeonse home

explain_en: Use it to set a home apart from a '월세방' where you pay monthly rent, or from a home you own ('내 집'). Jeonse is a housing contract style particular to Korea, so it is better to remember it as 'jeonse' than as a translation.

examples.en: The bus is delayed because of an accident.
The delivery was delayed because the construction ran long.
Please tell me in advance if the schedule is delayed.

examples.ko: 눈 때문에 비행기 출발이 지체될 것 같아요.
examples.en: The flight departure seems likely to be delayed because of snow.
The delay was long, so I waited a lot.

examples.ko: 서류가 늦게 와서 일이 지체돼서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: The documents came late and the work is delayed, so I am worried.

explain: 지체되다는 있어야 할 시간보다 늦어질 때 써요. 주어는 일정, 배송, 교통처럼 일의 진행이에요. 사람이 약속에 늦는 건 '늦다'나 '지각하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The bus was delayed because of traffic, so I was late.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말하고 다음 이야기로 이어 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give a reason and continue the sentence.

phrases.en: The schedule was delayed because of the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일의 진행이 늦어질 때 '일정'과 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with '일정' when progress of work runs late.

phrases.en: I'll send it quickly so the delivery isn't delayed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 늦어지지 않게 하려는 목적을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state the aim of avoiding delay.
phrases.en_equiv: so as not to be delayed

explain_en: 지체되다 is for things that run later than they should; the subject is a schedule, delivery, traffic or other process. For a person being late to an appointment, use '늦다' or '지각하다'.

examples.ko: 지방지 기자가 현장을 가장 먼저 확인했다.
examples.en: The local newspaper reporter was the first to check the scene.

examples.ko: 이 도시에서는 지방지가 지역 소식을 가장 자세히 다뤄요.
examples.en: In this city, the local paper covers regional news in the most detail.

examples.ko: 지방지는 큰 신문사가 다루지 않는 동네 이야기를 기사로 쓴다.
examples.en: Local papers write articles on neighborhood stories that big newspapers don't cover.

examples.ko: 지방지 구독자가 줄어서 문을 닫는 신문사도 있어요.
examples.en: Some newspapers are closing because their local-paper subscribers have dwindled.

examples.ko: 아버지는 고향에서 나오는 지방지를 매일 아침 읽으세요.
examples.en: My father reads the local newspaper from his hometown every morning.

explain: '지방지'는 서울이 아닌 지역에서 나오는 신문이에요. 전국에 나오는 신문은 '전국지', 서울에서 나오는 큰 신문은 '중앙지'라고 불러요.

dict_examples.ko: 낯선 고장으로 여행을 갔을 때 그 지방의 지방지를 보면 대충 그 지방색을 알 수 있다.
dict_examples.en: When you travel to an unfamiliar area, you can get a rough sense of the local character by looking at that region's local newspaper.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 지방지 is a newspaper published outside Seoul. A paper distributed nationwide is a 전국지, and the big Seoul-based papers are called 중앙지.

en: to attend (class, work); to be present (attendance)

examples.en: I attend class every day.
I was sick yesterday, so I couldn't attend.
Be sure to attend on the day of the exam.
We give a small gift to students who attend.
All the students are present today.
If you come every day, they give you a stamp.

explain: 학교·학원 수업에 나오는 건 '출석하다'이고, 회의나 결혼식 같은 행사에 가는 건 '참석하다'를 많이 써요. 반대말은 '결석하다'이고, 늦게 오면 '지각하다'예요. 선생님이 이름을 불러 확인하는 건 '출석을 부르다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Everyone attended class today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 수업에 나온 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used for having attended class.

phrases.en: I did not attend class yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 나오지 않았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say you did not come.

phrases.en: The teacher takes attendance every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선생님이 이름을 불러 누가 왔는지 확인할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for a teacher calling names to check who is present.

explain_en: Showing up for school or academy classes is 출석하다, while going to events such as meetings or weddings is usually '참석하다'. The opposite is '결석하다' (be absent), and arriving late is '지각하다'. A teacher calling names to check is '출석을 부르다'.

dis.h: be present in class; roll call

p.n: 출석 means being counted present; 참석 means taking part in it.

examples.en: I left my charging cable behind.
The cable is short, so it doesn't reach the bed.
The cable connection is wrong.
I replaced the TV cable at home.

examples.ko: 이 케이블은 컴퓨터와 모니터를 이어 줘요.
examples.en: This cable connects the computer and the monitor.

examples.ko: 책상 뒤 케이블에 걸려서 넘어질 뻔했어요.
examples.en: I almost tripped on a cable behind the desk.

explain: 충전 케이블, USB 케이블처럼 기기를 잇는 줄에 많이 써요. 일상에서는 그냥 '선'이라고도 해요. '케이블카', '케이블 TV'처럼 다른 말과 합쳐지기도 해요.

phrases.en: The charging cable is broken.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰이나 기기를 충전하는 줄을 말할 때 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, for the cord that charges a phone or device.

phrases.en: I connected the cable to the computer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기기를 줄로 이을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for joining devices with a cord.

phrases.en: We watch cable TV at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄로 연결해서 보는 TV 방송을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: TV service delivered through a cable.

explain_en: It is commonly used for wires that connect devices, like a charging cable or USB cable. In daily talk people also just say 선. It also joins other words, as in 케이블카 and 케이블 TV.
